title: Ferroni 2026 · Experiment 2 · Motor effector
citation: Ferroni, F., Rastelli, F., Langiulli, N., Rinaldi, L. S., Gallese, V., & Ardizzi, M. (2026). Dealing with the world close to our body. Characterizing determinants of peripersonal space plasticity. Neuropsychologia, 229, 109490.
notes: Inspect the hand-effector group timing as two 20-trial software examples. The full repetition count, foot-effector group and physical tool training remain outside this preview.

published_method.analysis: Estimate between-distance PPS location (PSE) and steepness (DL) using Spearman–Kärber on participant-level 10% trimmed reaction time means. Compare session and assigned group with a participant random intercept.

hand_assessment.cue: 3 s pink noise at 44.1 kHz, exponential nominal gain rise from 55 to 70 dB for looming, flat level 62.5 dB. The near and far loudspeaker gains change in opposite directions.
hand_assessment.response: Left-hand keyboard reaction to a right-index electrocutaneous pulse, with no response for auditory-only catches.

published_method.foot_assessment: Assess the dorsal right foot with floor-level loudspeakers and foot-directed acoustic motion, as shown in Figure 2. Foot stimulation device and exact source geometry are unreported.
published_method.training: Hand participants transfer cubes with the right-hand gripper. Foot participants wear a rod and push the cubes with the trained foot. Each completes 100 movements.

stimulus_type.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher Fig. 2, experimental setup; Ferroni et al. 2026, mmc1.docx, PPS control analyses, §2.2

source_provenance.value: Neuropsychologia 229 (2026), article 109490, publisher version of record

trajectory_count.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §§2–3 (pp. 2–7), Figs. 1–4
trajectory_count.gap: Approach geometry varies by group. Audio assessments also include a stationary control.

value.Hand Effector: Frontal apparent sound approach with near speaker about 10 cm from the right hand and far speaker 100 cm from the participant's body, via explicit Experiment 1 procedure reuse.
value.Foot Effector: Auditory stimulus approaches the same right foot receiving the tactile pulse. Its two floor-level speakers are schematic.

trajectory_path.source: Ferroni et al. (2026), Neuropsychologia 229:109490, final issue pp. 3–4, §§2.1.2 and 2.2.2 and Fig. 2.
trajectory_path.gap: Speaker distances use different bodily references. Perceived trajectory coordinates, exact Foot layout and calibrated distance-versus-time curves are unreported.

stimulus_duration.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §§2.2.1–2 (Experiment 2)
stimulus_duration.gap: The hand protocol explicitly repeats Experiment 1. No separate foot waveform verification.

stimulus_speed.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2 (pp. 2–6)
stimulus_speed.gap: No common value is specified across the four experiments. See the condition-specific Methods and standing code evidence.

Foot Effector: Auditory approach to the right foot
Unisensory tactile comparison reported in the Experiment 2 control

auditory_conditions.source: Ferroni et al. (2026), Neuropsychologia 229:109490, final issue pp. 3–4, §§2.1.2 and 2.2.2 and Fig. 2. Original publisher mmc1.docx, PPS control analyses §2.2.
auditory_conditions.gap: The source does not give a separate Foot flat-sound assignment or the Foot-specific condition quotas. The controls are reported for Experiment 2 as a whole.

value.Hand Effector: Looming sound has an exponentially increasing nominal level. Far output decreases from its maximum toward silence while near output rises from its minimum to its maximum.

gain_envelope.source: Ferroni et al. (2026), Neuropsychologia 229:109490, final issue pp. 3–4, §§2.1.2 and 2.2.2 and Fig. 2.
gain_envelope.gap: Per-channel gain coefficients, SPL calibration and Foot playback envelopes are unreported.

value.Hand Effector: Experiment 1 two-speaker audio setup and Digitimer DS3 electrical pulse through paired electrodes on the hairy surface of the right index finger.
value.Foot Effector: Electrical stimulation on the dorsal right foot. Figure 2 depicts two floor-level speakers.

renderer_or_apparatus.source: Ferroni et al. (2026), Neuropsychologia 229:109490, final issue pp. 3–4, §§2.1.2 and 2.2.2 and Fig. 2.
renderer_or_apparatus.gap: The exact Foot stimulator, electrode configuration, channel mapping and acoustic calibration remain unreported.

trial_rows_families.source: Ferroni et al. (2026), Neuropsychologia 229:109490, final issue pp. 3–4, §§2.1.2 and 2.2.2 and Fig. 2. Original publisher mmc1.docx, PPS control analyses §2.2.
trial_rows_families.gap: Hand values are percentages for the documented reused assessment. Exact Foot family quotas and within-block counts are unavailable.

condition_intermixing.value: The mixed design assigns one group per participant and repeats assessment pre/post.
condition_intermixing.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2 (p. 2)
condition_intermixing.gap: Within-session stimulus intermixing and randomization algorithm are unreported.

blocked_or_random_order.value: Random assignment to groups with the same fixed session order.
blocked_or_random_order.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2 (p. 2)
blocked_or_random_order.gap: Within-session order and blocking remain unreported.

iti_jitter_policy.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2 (p. 2)
iti_jitter_policy.gap: The reviewed experiment methods supply no exact ITI and jitter schedule.

response_window.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2 (p. 2)
response_window.gap: Exact accepted RT window and online timeout are unreported in the article. A standing analysis example uses input-table filtering.

task_sequence_rules.value: Pre-training PPS assessment, motor tool training, post-training PPS assessment. Approximately 10 minutes per session. The tool is absent from the two assessment sessions.
task_sequence_rules.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2 (p. 2)

tactile_stimulus.value: Right index finger (hand group) or dorsal right foot (foot group). Sound approaches the tested effector. Electrical stimulation.
tactile_stimulus.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §§2.2.1–2 (Experiment 2)
tactile_stimulus.gap: Exact foot electrode positions, hardware settings and pulse width unreported.

soa_table.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §§2.2.1–2 (Experiment 2) and publisher Fig. 5
soa_table.gap: Foot grid verified against the plotted times. Foot trigger log unavailable.

baseline_strategy.value: Touch-only baseline and multimodal facilitation comparison.
baseline_strategy.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2.1.2 (pp. 3–4)
baseline_strategy.gap: The hand group explicitly repeats Experiment 1. The foot group changes effector and approach target.

baseline_timing.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2.1.2 (pp. 3–4)
baseline_timing.gap: Explicit for Hand via §2.1.2. Foot baseline timing is unreported separately.

catch_trial_type.value: Looming or flat sound with no tactile pulse.
catch_trial_type.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2.1.2 (pp. 3–4)
catch_trial_type.gap: Explicit for Hand via §2.1.2. Foot catch schedule is unreported separately.

repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §§2.2.1–2 (Experiment 2)
repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.gap: The reviewed main methods do not report assessment repetitions by onset.

baseline_count.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §3 (pp. 6–7)
baseline_count.gap: The documented audio protocol supplies a baseline share without an exact trial total.

catch_count.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §3 (pp. 6–7)
catch_count.gap: The documented audio protocol supplies a catch share without an exact trial total. The visual allocation is unreported.

block_count.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §2 (p. 2)
block_count.gap: Blocks per assessment session are unreported.

total_trial_count.source: Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §3 (pp. 6–7)
total_trial_count.gap: Exact assessment totals are unreported. Training transfers and supplement input-row requirements have separate meanings.

implementation_gaps: Exact trial counts, block sizes, intertrial timing and response windows per assessment group are unreported.
Validate both assessments and the intervening physical training with the corresponding cohort and original geometry. Original realized trial sequences and participant analysis inputs are unavailable.
Recover foot-specific stimulation hardware, timing and foot-centered speaker placement. Calibrate the electrocutaneous and dual-speaker outputs for both effectors.

software_preview_allocation.reason: The 20-trial demonstrator is the smallest integer 50:40:10 allocation covering one occurrence of each of the two waveforms at each of the five target SOAs. Published allocation per waveform, target SOA and phase is unreported.
software_preview_allocation.provisional_choices: Equal catch distribution across the sound options. The helper’s 1000 ms audio-reference offset and trailing placeholder silence are toolkit timing choices.

reference_parameters.preview_source: Ardizzi–Ferri synthesized 3 s pink-noise files show digital looming and flat examples. The published physical cross-fade and individual calibration require lab verification.
reference_parameters.preview_scope: A qualifying audio-tactile timing unit for the hand-effector group, shown once in pre- and once in post-training order. The original number of trials and exact allocations remain unresolved.

provenance.source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuropsychologia.2026.109490. Ferroni et al. 2026, publisher version of record, §§2.2.1–2 (Experiment 2)
